title: Is The AI Capex Surge A Threat To Amazon Stock?
detail:
Is The AI Capex Surge A Threat To Amazon Stock?
Trefis Team
Thu, September 10, 2026 at 2:06 PM EDT 3 min read
AMZN
NFLX
GOOG
MSFT
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Amazon.com (AMZN) plans to spend roughly $220 billion of cash on capital in 2026, against $775.7 billion of revenue over the trailing twelve months. The sheer size of that bill introduces notable capital allocation and cash flow pressures that investors must weigh. The rest is who sets the number, and how long the money has to stay out before any of it comes back.

Amazon Is Outspending Its Own Profits

In the second quarter of 2026 Amazon put $53.1 billion of cash into capital spending, close to twice the $27.5 billion of operating income it earned in the same quarter. Most of that money goes to AWS and generative AI. The money buys data centers, and it buys the servers and networking equipment that fill them. Those two halves of the bill behave very differently.

And Amazon Has Already Raised That Bill Once

Earlier in 2026 the plan was about $200 billion. Management raised it for one stated reason: the higher cost of memory. One component moved the 2026 capital plan by about $20 billion. By the company's own read, memory and hard drive prices across the industry are inflated.

Through 2028 there is no year in which Amazon can pause and wait for those prices to settle. Management says demand has already reserved the lion's share of 2027 capacity, and quite a bit of 2028 capacity too. Demand that far out is a good problem to have. It is also a commitment to keep buying components at those prices for as long as that demand holds.

So When Does Amazon Get It Back?

Not soon, on management's own schedule. Data center capital goes out starting two years before servers can be installed and start earning, and those data centers then carry 30-plus-year useful lives. The servers themselves have useful lives of at least five to six years, and it takes a little under three years on average to break even on them. That server hardware is bought only a few months before going into service on visible demand. While data center shells sit idle for the two years required to construct them, the servers' sub-three-year break-even clock begins immediately once they are installed. Management has been direct about the consequence: free cash flow runs into headwinds until the data centers come online and can be monetized.

You Are Not Waiting On Demand

AWS revenue grew 36.7% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, the fifth straight quarter that growth has sped up, and the backlog stands at $496 billion. Amazon is not building into thin air. What a holder is waiting on is the bill itself.

title: Is IBM Stock A Buy After Missing On Transaction Processing?
detail:
Is IBM Stock A Buy After Missing On Transaction Processing?
Trefis Team
Thu, September 10, 2026 at 1:43 PM EDT 3 min read
IBM
AMZN
ORCL
GOOG
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Photo by Mohamed_hassan on Pixabay

International Business Machines (IBM) has given back 12.9% over the past three months and sits at $239.94, about 73% of its 52-week high. Management sees no evidence of clients moving off the mainframe. What has changed is that a key slice of IBM's transactional software revenue rides on a purchase those clients have learned they can postpone.

IBM Did Not Close The Deals It Was Counting On In June

Revenue grew 1% in the June quarter at constant currency. Transaction processing revenue fell 9% on that basis, while data grew 18% and automation grew 3%. Tens of large deals failed to close on the timelines the company expected, and they accounted for most of the shortfall.

Revenue over the past twelve months still reads $69.1 billion, up 7.9%, because that window carries three quarters that grew above 9%. The June quarter itself grew 1.1% as reported.

The vulnerability lies in where the revenue shortfall occurred. About 80% of IBM's software revenue is recurring, and it grew nicely. The other 20% is transactional, sold through enterprise license agreements that clients buy alongside mainframe hardware and book as capital spending. Those agreements typically carry a heavy concentration of transaction processing software, though they can also include data and automation products. The CFO puts the multiplier at more than $3 of software for every dollar of hardware landed.

But IBM Was Not The Most Urgent Bill To Pay

In the final weeks of June, management says, clients redirected spending towards servers, storage and memory purchases to secure supply-constrained infrastructure ahead of expected price increases. By the CEO's account, some of those alternate purchases were rising 30% in dollar value quarter to quarter, so budget went where prices were climbing fastest.

IBM held its own price through the first weeks of July, management says, and is less aggressive on increases than the alternate infrastructure providers. That is defensible. It also hands the timing of IBM's software revenue to an infrastructure price surge the company has chosen not to match.

So How Long Can IBM Wait For That Money?

Longer than one quarter. About a third of the slipped deals closed within three weeks of the June quarter ending, which is management's case for deferral rather than destruction. With transactional software depressed, analysts increasingly view Transaction Processing as a potential 2027 rebound rather than a 2026 driver.

By the CFO's description, clients capable of purchasing via monthly license charges (MLC) can run on an operating-expense model without a big purchase for three years, though he adds that the upgrade cycle eventually catches them and moves in IBM's favor. Three years is long enough for a risk to arrive without ever looking like an event.

title: Should You Buy Meta Stock For Cash Flow It Plans To Spend?
detail:
Should You Buy Meta Stock For Cash Flow It Plans To Spend?
Trefis Team
Thu, September 10, 2026 at 1:18 PM EDT 3 min read
META
^GSPC
SPGI
AMZN
PINS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Photo by flutie8211 on Pixabay

Meta Platforms (META) trades at about $653, roughly 16% below its 52-week high, and at 11.3 times operating cash flow against 15.2 for the S&P 500. A discount of this scale on a business delivering 28% top-line growth presents a notable valuation divergence, though one largely explained by the company's surging capital commitments. The cash flow that multiple is priced on is money Meta plans to spend.

Why Is Meta Cheaper Than The Market On Cash Flow?

The cash is real. Meta turned 57.1% of revenue into operating cash flow over the trailing twelve months, against 21.9% for the market. Family of Apps ad revenue grew 27% in the June 2026 quarter, with impressions up 14% and the average price per ad up 12%.

More inventory sold at higher prices is a healthy ad market, though management credited the price gain partly to currency tailwinds. WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions pushed quarterly Family of Apps other revenue to $1 billion for the first time. Nothing in the advertising engine explains a discount to the S&P 500 on cash flow.

Where Is Meta Putting All That Cash?

Into concrete and chips. Capital expenditures, including finance leases, ran $31.1 billion in the June 2026 quarter, and free cash flow came to $784 million on $60.8 billion of revenue. Management guides 2026 capital expenditures, including finance leases, to $130 billion to $145 billion, against operating cash flow of about $130.3 billion over the trailing twelve months.

A full-year plan against a trailing window is only an approximation. At the midpoint of 2026 guidance, projected full-year capital expenditures would nearly match the company's trailing twelve-month operating cash flow.

A venture with BlackRock is putting a 1 gigawatt data center in El Paso, Texas, and management plans to add as much capacity as it can in 2026 and 2027.

What Happens To You If The Build Outruns The Ads?

Meta is not funding the build out of the business alone. Management says its balance sheet lets it attract outside capital to supplement the cash the business generates. The June 2026 quarter closed with $90.3 billion in cash and marketable securities against $83.7 billion of debt. GAAP operating income fell 8% to $18.8 billion, but $2.4 billion of legal charges and $1.2 billion of May 2026 severance sit inside that decline. Without them, operating income would have risen 9%, though Meta explicitly notes in its regulatory filings that ongoing U.S. multi-district litigation concerning youth platform usage poses a risk of material financial loss.

Polymarket named Warren Jenson as its first chief financial officer on Thursday, bringing in a veteran finance executive as the prediction markets company expands its U.S. platform.

Jenson built his early career as finance chief at Amazon, Electronic Arts, Delta Air Lines, and NBC, a run of high-profile roles that stretched across the 1990s and into the early 2000s, according to the Wall Street Journal. He will report to Polymarket founder and CEO Shayne Coplan, the company said.

In the role, Jenson will lead Polymarket's finance organization, set financial and capital strategy, and build infrastructure to support the company's next phase of growth, the company said.

His most recent post was president and CFO of Nielsen, a position he departed in January 2025, according to the Wall Street Journal. Prior to that, he logged more than four years as president and CFO at the data platform LiveRamp, overseeing its finances and heading up its international operations. He also serves on the boards of DigitalOcean, Dropbox, and Ripple, the company said.

"We're assembling the team to match the opportunity in front of us," Coplan said in a statement. "Warren has led finance at some of the most consequential companies in the world, and his experience will be critical to everything we build from here."

"I'm joining Shayne and the leadership team to put the capital strategy and operating discipline in place to move quickly at scale," Jenson said in a statement.

The appointment comes as Polymarket scales its U.S. exchange, which operates as a designated contract market regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. Polymarket also added Travis VanderZanden, the founder of a scooter-sharing company, as chief growth officer earlier this year, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Polymarket is valued at around $21 billion after a recent $1 billion fundraise. 1789 Capital — the venture and growth equity firm where Donald Trump Jr. holds a partner role — is putting roughly $300 million into the company. Intercontinental Exchange has also emerged as a major backer, having disclosed a $1.6 billion position in the company earlier this year, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Polymarket and Kalshi have been locked in a battle for dominance in the prediction markets sector, a contest that has grown more crowded as Robinhood and DraftKings have each rolled out their own offerings in the space.

title: Can Apple's Foldable iPhone Fuel the Next Growth Cycle for the Stock?
detail:
Can Apple's Foldable iPhone Fuel the Next Growth Cycle for the Stock?
Aniruddha Ganguly
Thu, September 10, 2026 at 12:49 PM EDT 6 min read
AAPL
GOOGL
AMZN
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Apple AAPL has expanded its flagship smartphone portfolio with the iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone, opening a new product category that could strengthen the company's upgrade cycle and deepen engagement across its hardware, AI and services ecosystem. The launch comes against a strong backdrop for iPhone, which generated $54.3 billion in third-quarter fiscal 2026 (June quarter) revenues, up 22% year over year.

The foldable iPhone could provide Apple with another important catalyst for upgrades. Apple's iPhone installed base reached an all-time high in the June quarter, while the company also recorded a June-quarter record for upgraders. With more than 2.5 billion active Apple devices globally, the company has a substantial customer base to which it can introduce the differentiated foldable form factor.

Will the foldable iPhone boost investor confidence in Apple stock? Let's find out.

iPhone Duo: A Snapshot of the Features

Apple's iPhone Duo combines a 5.4-inch outer Super Retina XDR display with a 7.6-inch inner display that is 50% larger than the iPhone 18 Pro Max. Apple has designed the device to offer a conventional smartphone experience when closed while providing a larger canvas for content consumption, gaming and productivity when opened. The displays support ProMotion and Always On functionality, while Apple Pencil support is expected later this year.

The foldable design also gives Apple an opportunity to differentiate the iPhone experience through software. iOS 27 brings Split View to iPhone, allowing users to operate two applications side by side, open multiple windows and save frequently used app combinations. Netflix, Zoom and Slack are already adapting their applications for the foldable form factor, which should help broaden productivity and entertainment use cases and strengthen developer support for the new device.

Apple is pairing the new form factor with its expanding AI capabilities. iPhone Duo incorporates Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, including personal-context understanding, onscreen awareness and privacy-focused processing through on-device computing and Private Cloud Compute. The A20 Pro chip features a dual 16-core Neural Engine with twice the compute capability for on-device AI models, 50% more unified memory bandwidth and advanced thermal management for demanding AI and multitasking workloads.

Can Foldable iPhone Boost Apple's Prospects?

The launch of the foldable iPhone bodes well for Apple's prospects. iPhone sales have been benefiting from higher shipments of premium Pro models. The introduction of another highly differentiated device could therefore help sustain demand among customers seeking premium features and potentially strengthen Apple's product mix. Apple Upgrade could further support adoption. The recently launched U.S. leasing program is intended to make the company's latest products more affordable for customers who prefer to upgrade on a regular schedule, with early feedback described as positive.

iPhone Duo is also expected to strengthen Apple's Services opportunity. The company ended the latest quarter with more than 1.5 billion paid subscriptions, while Services revenues increased 12% year over year to $30.7 billion. A larger display optimized for multitasking, video, apps and AI could increase engagement across the App Store, iCloud and other services. Apple has also indicated that heavy Siri AI users may eventually have opportunities to move to higher iCloud Plus plans, creating an additional monetization avenue.

Although Apple expects high iPhone demand, it has warned that supply constraints affecting advanced-node chips are limiting iPhone, Mac and iPad availability. Memory costs are also rising. These factors could restrict Apple's ability to fully capitalize on initial iPhone Duo demand. In fact, the memory shortage and rising prices have been blamed for declining global smartphone sales, which dropped 7% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, per Counterpoint Research. Samsung reclaimed the global leadership position with a 23% market share and growing 9% year over year, while Apple recorded 13% year-over-year growth and its highest Q2 market share (21%), driven by the continued strength of the iPhone 17 series.
